conclusion: No unresolved engineering blocker found in the final recorded snapshot. Four issues/fixture defects were resolved; one overbroad review claim was withdrawn. This is offline review, not online source-coverage or accuracy acceptance.

findings.problem: The binary-dispatch diagnostic selected an existing-block replacement slot, which could not add blocks or rewire/remove edges needed to correct the topology.
findings.resolution: Only cfg/binary_dispatch uses the existing whole-object correction, inside the same single correction budget; other record corrections remain unchanged.
findings.verification: test_binary_dispatch_correction_can_add_needed_block_and_rewire_once; corrected topology and zero-model-call replay both pass.

findings.problem: Callback-only reproduction showed OSError escaping the callback. The review initially inferred it could terminate analysis without checking the existing runner.mark exception boundary.
findings.resolution: The existing runner already isolates ordinary observer Exceptions and preserves KeyboardInterrupt. Remove the redundant new callback wrapper; no new observation mechanism is needed.
findings.verification: Final seven-call orchestration deliberately raises progress OSError and still completes with matching zero-call fixture replay. The callback-level test confirms errors reach the existing caller boundary. Original callback reproduction remains but does not establish an analysis failure.

findings.scope: existing backend issue exposed by 013 regression
findings.problem: Demand seeding tried to resolve local producers on instructions already proven not_reached, despite existing handling of inactive paths elsewhere.
findings.resolution: Goals remain declared; exact not_reached targets produce nonblocking inactive_goal and no seed. They do not enter bound_goals. Unmodeled/blocked targets remain unresolved, and requirements with only inactive goals retain blocking unbound_requirement.
findings.verification: Both inactive-goal regressions pass; the independent all-inactive-R1 check returned partial with has_applicable_goal=false and retained unbound_requirement. The JSON is explicitly post-fix evidence, not a pre-fix reproduction.

findings.problem: The 013 fixture briefly inserted a source-unsupported explicit read to initialize an append destination.
findings.resolution: Remove the invented read. Explicit scenario states seed unknown prior storage; the ordinary no-initial-state path uses existing production acquisition of unknown prior storage. No engine change was needed.
findings.verification: test_013_default_initial_state_keeps_unknown_previous_log_without_invented_read and the final 013 regression subset pass.

findings.problem: Early KeyboardInterrupt before runner terminal-state handling could leave result prepared/running while the controller wrote a finished marker with status null. The queue previously accepted this marker and launched the next case.
findings.resolution: The queue now requires terminal statuses in both controller-finished and result, and explicitly stops for controller KeyboardInterrupt. Ordinary terminal failures still continue.
findings.verification: Eight fake-subprocess/temp-directory scenarios passed; no actual process or run was started.

confirmed_properties: Full frozen source reaches current CFG and each semantic fragment, including semantic rebuilds; Task/mapping/sensitivity isolation and exact duplicate-code omission remain.
New binary topology diagnostics have a usable one-correction path; source-review cfg versus processing ownership follows the existing dependency closure.
Model-side omitted write.mode is normalized to explicit replace; the raw backend still requires mode and explicit append/delete semantics remain.
Empty subset/map proofs follow finite content alternatives conservatively; opaque, cyclic and unknown bases do not establish emptiness.
Completed material/index reuse is retained; no persistent cache, call-stack, exception engine or extra semantic stage was introduced.
Preparation and queue are limited to root-owned four fresh cases in GA4/001/010/013 order; each controller owns one replay, timing observation adds no model call.
limits: Authored regression candidates prove representability and deterministic behavior, not that a model will generate correct candidates.
Full-source input can reach the existing transport character limit; no arbitrary-size support or automatic slicing is claimed.
Compiled combined examples increase some prompt views; actual token/latency benefit and useful source-boundary coverage require the authorized fresh validation.
Review acceptance is scoped to the recorded hashes. Root retains sole dispatch ownership and must complete overall offline acceptance before launch.
